oerbier.title: Oerbier | Dark, top-fermented beer from De Dolle Brouwers, Esen (Belgium)
oerbier.description: Oerbier (9%) is the first beer of De Dolle Brouwers, a craft brewery in Esen, West Flanders. A dark beer with seven kinds of malt and whole-cone hops from Poperinge, unfiltered and refermented in the bottle.
oerbier.intro: The very first beer of the brewery, officially brewed since 15 November 1980. Seven kinds of malt, a complex yeast and whole-cone hops from Poperinge. Unfiltered and refermented in the bottle.

notes.label: Aroma
notes.text: Rich, yeasty and darkly malty, with a light fruity touch.

notes.label: Taste
notes.text: Rich, complex flavours in balance. The sweet malt has the upper hand, with lightly hoppy, bitter and slightly sour notes.

notes.label: Finish
notes.text: Full-bodied and floral.

info.label: Serving tip
info.text: Keep cool and dark in the cellar and pour at 12°C into the Oerbier glass or a wine glass.

info.label: Keeping
info.text: Keeps for at least two years, but Oerbier keeps evolving and can be cellared much longer.

weetjes: De Dolle Brouwers started out as De Dolle Dravers, a cycling club with four members.
Oerbier was perfected over three years in a copper washtub over a wood fire.
At a blind tasting in the Brouwershuis it came out as the best.
The year 1980 refers to the first official brew, on 15 November 1980. It was the start of a revival of special beers in Belgium.
Take a good look at the logo on the glass: it's not a lady, a monk or a king, but a personified yeast cell.
After a few years of ageing Oerbier takes on a wine-like character.
The brewery still keeps samples of the very first brew, and they are still perfectly drinkable.
"Nat en straf" (wet and strong) on the glasses is a warning about the 9%.
The Oerbier figure holds a brewer's fork, the work, but looks at the glass of beer, the result.
On the metal signs the Oerbier figure rides a wild beast, after the cave drawings of Altamira in Spain, from around 15,000 BC.
oerbier.tagline: Our first beer. Dark, with seven kinds of malt.

arabier.title: Arabier | Blond, dry-hopped beer from De Dolle Brouwers, Esen (Belgium)
arabier.description: Arabier (8%) from De Dolle Brouwers is the blond sister of Oerbier, from Esen (West Flanders). Brewed with pale malt and dry-hopped with whole-cone hops from Poperinge. Fresh, fruity and bitter.
arabier.intro: Plenty of beer lovers liked Oerbier, but also asked for a pale beer. So came Arabier: brewed with a single malt, pale malt, and a bitterness that keeps the taste in balance.

notes.label: Aroma
notes.text: Fruity, fresh and bitter, from the WGV hops (Whitbread Golding Variety).

notes.label: Taste
notes.text: Dry and fresh, with a Nugget hop bitterness that balances the pale malt.

notes.label: Finish
notes.text: Long and bitter, refreshing to the last sip.

info.label: Serving tip
info.text: Drink Arabier cool, at 10 °C, as it says in Arabic on the bottle.

info.label: Keeping
info.text: Keeps for two years; the date is on the crown cap.

weetjes: Beer is beer, but it had to start with an A. So Arabier it was: ideal after an afternoon walking in the desert.
The label shows a colourful parrot, a macaw ("ara" in Dutch).
The bottle says in Arabic: "Drink cool, 10 °C".
The hop cones grow around Poperinge. They are dried, pressed and added to the wort like that.
In Dutch the name is always written with a small a.
One arabier, two arabiers. But there are never two Arabs ("arabieren").
A wink: in Arab countries beer is actually forbidden.
arabier.tagline: The blond sister of Oerbier, dry-hopped.

stille-nacht.title: Stille Nacht | Christmas beer from De Dolle Brouwers, Esen (Belgium)
stille-nacht.description: Stille Nacht (12%) is the Christmas beer and prestige beer of De Dolle Brouwers from Esen, West Flanders. Voted best Christmas beer many times at the Christmas beer festival in Essen, Belgium.
stille-nacht.intro: Our prestige beer, with every trump card on the table: 1,000 kg of malt for 2,500 litres of beer, pale candi sugar and whole-cone hops from Poperinge (Whitbread Golding Variety). A very long boil, long lagering and refermentation in the bottle. Good for 22° Plato and 12%. At Christmas it can be a little more!

notes.label: Aroma
notes.text: Ripe fruit and candi sugar.

notes.label: Taste
notes.text: Full and sweetish, carried by the high gravity.

notes.label: Finish
notes.text: Warming and long.

info.label: Serving tip
info.text: Pour it slowly into the Oerbier glass or a wine glass, and take your time.

info.label: Keeping
info.text: Stille Nacht ages well. The bottling date is on the crown cap.

weetjes: In 1980 there were no Christmas beers in Belgium, apart from six English ones.
The name Stille Nacht ("Silent Night") came out of a brainstorm with brother Ward. He is the spiritual father of the name.
Boiled in a copper kettle over a direct gas flame and cooled in the copper coolship from 1921.
Fermented in open copper fermenters, then matured for at least a month.
Refermented in the bottle.
We brew one batch a day.

story.alt: Christmas card from De Dolle Brouwers: the Stille Nacht figure in the snow by the brewery, with the Dulle Teve on her broom, the macaw and the Boskeun
story.title: A new Christmas card every year
story.text: Every year around Christmas, Benjamin Herteleer draws a new Christmas card with the characters Kris once drew for the labels: the Stille Nacht figure, the Oerbier figure, the Dulle Teve, the Arabier macaw and the Boskeun. Glass in hand, ready for the season's greetings. The new card always appears on @dedollebrouwers.

extra.alt: Christmas drawing: Santa with a bottle of Stille Nacht and a Christmas tree with a glass in the Oerbar, with the characters from the labels
New Year drawing: three Oerbier figures riding bison in the snow with a "See you in 2025" flag

prijzen.title: The best Christmas beer in Belgium
prijzen.text: Every year the beer tasters of OBER in Essen (near Antwerp) hold a festival with nothing but Belgian Christmas beers. Since 1994 the visitors pick their favourite there, out of more than 200 beers. No expert jury: the beers are bought and poured anonymously. Stille Nacht nearly always ends up in the top 3. Since 2005 it has received the certificate for best Christmas beer eleven times, and it already won in the years before that, when no certificates were handed out yet. It also came second or third several times, Stille Nacht Reserva included. The certificates hang in the Oerbar.

boskeun.title: Boskeun | Easter beer with honey from De Dolle Brouwers, Esen (Belgium)
boskeun.description: Boskeun (9%) is the Easter beer of De Dolle Brouwers from Esen (West Flanders), brewed with honey and Golding hops from Poperinge.
boskeun.kicker: One of the first Easter beers
boskeun.intro: Our Easter beer of 9%, following Stille Nacht in the year. The unique ingredient is honey, one of the oldest sweeteners for drinks. Soft in taste, with a fruity aroma.

notes.label: Aroma
notes.text: Fruity, with a touch of honey.

notes.label: Taste
notes.text: Soft, with the round sweetness of the honey.

notes.label: Finish
notes.text: Long and soft.

info.label: Serving tip
info.text: Pour it into the Oerbier glass or a tulip glass.

weetjes: Easter beer has been a thing in Belgium only since 1982. Before that there was just the Easter beer of Slaghmuylder, a stronger pils.
"Boskeun" is West Flemish for wild rabbit. A rabbit is cuddly, sweet and soft, and sometimes the nickname of a sweet lady.
Brewed with pale malt, Golding hops from Poperinge, organic cane sugar, honey and pure spring water.
Honey is one of the oldest sweeteners for drinks.
Unfiltered, unpasteurised and refermented in the bottle.
"Keun" was the nickname of Jo, one of the Herteleer brothers. After a brotherly fight he was left with a cut on his upper lip, a hare lip. That is how it became Boskeun.

story.alt: Illustration of the Boskeun rabbits in their underground bar
story.title: A new Boskeun every spring
story.text: We brew Boskeun once a year, for Easter. And every year Benjamin Herteleer, the youngest generation of the family, draws a new picture for it: the Boskeun rabbits in their underground local, at the Easter table or around a campfire in the woods, with a pot of honey of course. The batch usually sells out fast. Want to know when the new brew is in? Keep an eye on our socials: @dedollebrouwers.

extra.alt: Drawing of the Boskeun rabbits raising a glass at the Easter table
Drawing of the Boskeun rabbits around a campfire in the woods, with bees and a pot of honey

boskeun.tagline: One of the first Easter beers, with honey.

dulle-teve.title: Dulle Teve | Tripel from De Dolle Brouwers, Esen (Belgium)
dulle-teve.description: Dulle Teve (10%) is a tripel from De Dolle Brouwers in Esen, West Flanders, brewed with white candi sugar and with a witty story behind its name.
dulle-teve.intro: A golden tripel of 10%, brewed with white candi sugar in the kettle. The name was born in the Oerbar, when an impatient landlady snapped at her husband on the phone: "Do you know what you are? A dulle teve!" (a mad bitch) — and the brewers knew at once: name found, now we just have to brew the beer.

notes.label: Aroma
notes.text: Fruity, with a touch of candi sugar.

notes.label: Taste
notes.text: Full, with the sweetness of the white candi sugar.

notes.label: Finish
notes.text: Long and dry, with the 10% well hidden.

info.label: Serving tip
info.text: Pour at 10°C into the Oerbier glass or a tulip glass.

info.label: When
info.text: Available almost all year round.

info.label: Keeping
info.text: Best in a cool cellar.

weetjes: "Dulle teve" is dialect for a difficult woman.
The café owner who phoned was looking for a beer of his own and was tasting two beers at once in the Oerbar.
"Now we just need to make a beer, we already have the name."
A strong, smooth sipping beer, comparable to the Westmalle Tripel of 1936.

lichtervelds-blond.title: Lichtervelds Blond | Golden blond beer from De Dolle Brouwers, Esen (Belgium)
lichtervelds-blond.description: Lichtervelds Blond (8%) from De Dolle Brouwers is a golden blond beer, brewed in Esen, West Flanders.
lichtervelds-blond.kicker: Golden blond, once every two years
lichtervelds-blond.intro: A revived beer from Lichtervelde: originally "Blonde des Flandres" from brewery De Hoop / Th. Labens, now brewed and bottled by De Dolle Brouwers in Esen.

notes.label: Aroma
notes.text: Soft malt, a hint of citrus and discreet hops.

notes.label: Taste
notes.text: Round and full for a blond beer, with a soft sweetness that turns into a drier finish.

notes.label: Finish
notes.text: Fairly long and dry, with a subtle warmth from the alcohol.

info.label: Serving tip
info.text: Serve at 8-10°C in the Oerbier glass or a tulip glass.

info.label: Goes with
info.text: Light lunch dishes, mature cheese or as an aperitif.

weetjes: Brewed at the request of the local history society Karel Van de Poele in Lichtervelde.
On the market since 1990, each time for the Lichtervelde folklore festival held every two years.
Brewed only once every two years.
Taste, colour and strength vary slightly from batch to batch.
It has its own glass: a schwenker.

story.alt: Logo of brewery De Hoop, Lichtervelde
story.title: A revived local beer
story.text: The label refers to the original brewery "De Hoop" and maltings of Th. Labens in Lichtervelde (West Flanders), which once brewed this beer as "Blonde des Flandres". De Dolle Brouwers brews and bottles it again today in Esen, in the spirit of the original: pure malt and hops, unfiltered, refermented in the bottle.

export-stout.title: Export Stout | Stout from De Dolle Brouwers, Esen (Belgium)
export-stout.description: Export Stout (8%) from De Dolle Brouwers in Esen (West Flanders). Born when Guinness refused to brew a stout for our American importer, and every batch has a different recipe.
export-stout.intro: Our American importer B. United asked Guinness to brew a stout for them. Guinness refused, and Matthias of B. United asked whether we were interested. That's how we started brewing stout. The first stouts were a variation on Oerbier, with more roasted malt and candi sugar, at 9%. Today it is drier, without candi sugar, and 8%.

notes.label: Aroma
notes.text: Roasted malt.

notes.label: Taste
notes.text: Full and bitter, with dark malt.

notes.label: Finish
notes.text: Dry and bitter.

info.label: When
info.text: We brew it only a few times a year. Be quick.

info.label: Serving tip
info.text: Pour at 10-12°C into the Oerbier glass or a tulip glass.

info.label: Keeping
info.text: Keeps for two years.

weetjes: Stout used to be a beer the doctor prescribed, for instance when brother Ward had broken his leg.
Old stout labels said "recommended for invalids": for people getting back on their feet.
Every batch of stout gets a different recipe. We have a folder full of all the recipes.
The first labels and posters still say 9%. Today it is 8%.
The same fermentation as Oerbier.
It no longer goes to America. Every brewery there now makes its own stout, IPA, bourbon stout, vanilla stout, pastry stout with marshmallows, milkshake stout, and so on, and so on…

story.alt: Original label stamp of Export Stout, De Dolle Brouwers, Esen Belgium, 9%
story.title: The label
story.text: The round stamp on every bottle of Export Stout shows the brewery in Esen, with the brewer's signature. It still says 9%, as strong as the very first stouts. A classic, handmade design, fitting for a beer with just as few frills.

oeral.title: Oeral | Blond and bitter beer from De Dolle Brouwers, on draught only, Esen (Belgium)
oeral.description: Oeral (6%) is the lighter version of Arabier: blond and bitter. From De Dolle Brouwers in Esen, West Flanders, only on draught in the Oerbar.
oeral.intro: Oeral is a lighter version of Arabier, so blond and bitter. The name comes from "oer", pure, and "al", for everyone ("alleman"). We only pour it from the keg.

notes.label: Aroma
notes.text: Fresh whole-cone hops, just like Arabier.

notes.label: Taste
notes.text: Blond and bitter, but lighter than Arabier.

notes.label: Finish
notes.text: Dry and refreshing.

info.label: Serving tip
info.text: Only available on draught in the Oerbar. Served fresh.

weetjes: Oeral has a long and murky history.
It was first brewed for the first Arabier festival. Because drinking Arabier and water separately is fiction, and Arabier as a main course is a daring undertaking, even for trained beer lovers.
The label went from a little yellow plane to the Oeral building with hammer and sickle: Oeral as the far edge of Europe (the Urals), and the far edge of the art of beer…
Oeral doesn't keep long. Alcohol isn't just a cleaning product but also a preservative, and Oeral has less of it.
It's the only beer in our range that we don't bottle: it's purely for the Oerbar and the tap.
oeral.tagline: The lighter Arabier, only from the tap.

oerbier-reserva.title: Oerbier Reserva | Barrel-aged dark beer from De Dolle Brouwers, Esen (Belgium)
oerbier-reserva.description: Oerbier Reserva (9%) is the wine-barrel-aged version of Oerbier, from De Dolle Brouwers in Esen, West Flanders. Limited, numbered edition.
oerbier-reserva.intro: After twelve months in wine barrels, the dark base of Oerbier picks up notes of wood and wine.

notes.label: Aroma
notes.text: Red fruit, a hint of oak and the malty base of Oerbier.

notes.label: Taste
notes.text: Round and complex, with tannin and notes of wood and wine on top of the familiar Oerbier base.

notes.label: Finish
notes.text: Long, dry and slightly wine-like.

info.label: Serving tip
info.text: Serve at 12°C in a wine glass, so the wood notes can shine.

info.label: Goes with
info.text: Aged cheese, game or a dark chocolate dessert.

weetjes: We use wine barrels from France, Spain and Italy, and each barrel only once.
Every month we top up the barrels, so no air gets to the beer.
The label says which barrel the beer comes from, for example "barrique 11".
Store the bottles upright and cool.
Always a small edition.
The names Reserva and Gran Reserva come from the wine world, for wine aged in barrels. That's something different from the French Grand Cru.

barrel.title: About the barrel ageing
barrel.text: We have been ageing beer in wine barrels since 1996, and since 2000 there have been three Reservas: Oerbier, Dulle Teve and Stille Nacht. That makes De Dolle Brouwers one of the pioneers of barrel-aged beer in Belgium. Now and then a selected batch of Oerbier goes into wine barrels for at least a year, where it develops further and takes on notes of wood, wine and tannin, each time in a limited, numbered edition.

oerbier-reserva.tagline: Oerbier, at least a year in wine barrels.

dulle-teve-reserva.title: Dulle Teve Reserva | Barrel-aged tripel from De Dolle Brouwers, Esen (Belgium)
dulle-teve-reserva.description: Dulle Teve Reserva (10%) is the wine-barrel-aged version of Dulle Teve, the tripel of De Dolle Brouwers from Esen, West Flanders.
dulle-teve-reserva.kicker: Dulle Teve, aged in wine barrels
dulle-teve-reserva.intro: Extra round and warming: the tannins of the wine barrel add weight to the already sturdy Dulle Teve.

notes.label: Aroma
notes.text: Dark fruit, a hint of oak and the spicy kick of Dulle Teve.

notes.label: Taste
notes.text: Full and complex, with notes of wood and wine that soften the base.

notes.label: Finish
notes.text: Long, dry and slightly tannic.

info.label: Serving tip
info.text: Serve at 12°C in the Oerbier glass or a tulip glass and give it time to open up.

info.label: Goes with
info.text: Game, hearty stews or a sharp hard cheese.

weetjes: We use wine barrels from France, Spain and Italy, and each barrel only once.
Every month we top up the barrels, so no air gets to the beer.
The label says which barrel the beer comes from, for example "barrique 11".
Store the bottles upright and cool.
The names Reserva and Gran Reserva come from the wine world, for wine aged in barrels. That's something different from the French Grand Cru.

barrel.title: About the barrel ageing
barrel.text: Since 2000, now and then a selected batch of Dulle Teve also goes into wine barrels for at least a year. The tannins and wood notes give the beer an extra layer of complexity, each time in a limited, numbered edition.

dulle-teve-reserva.tagline: Our tripel, at least a year in wine barrels.

stille-nacht-reserva.title: Stille Nacht Reserva | Barrel-aged Christmas beer from De Dolle Brouwers, Esen (Belgium)
stille-nacht-reserva.description: Stille Nacht Reserva (12%) is the wine-barrel-aged version of Stille Nacht, released in limited editions by De Dolle Brouwers in Esen, West Flanders.
stille-nacht-reserva.kicker: Stille Nacht, aged for years in wine barrels
stille-nacht-reserva.intro: The complex, golden Stille Nacht gets a second life here: about two years in barrels that used to hold wine, into a deeper, woodier and slightly vinous beer of 12%. Not a yearly edition but a release every few years, each with its own barrel number.

notes.label: Aroma
notes.text: Oak, vanilla, dried fruit, citrus peel and a hint of wild yeast.

notes.label: Taste
notes.text: Lightly sour and fruity, with candied orange, wood and a soft vinous touch that trades the original Stille Nacht sweetness for more depth.

notes.label: Finish
notes.text: Long and warming, with the high strength well hidden behind wood and fruit.

info.label: Serving tip
info.text: Serve at 12°C in a wine glass — a bottle is meant for sharing on a special occasion.

info.label: Goes with
info.text: Aged cheese, a fruit dessert or simply on its own, to finish.

weetjes: We use wine barrels from France, Spain and Italy, and each barrel only once.
Every month we top up the barrels, so no air gets to the beer.
The label says which barrel the beer comes from, for example "barrique 11".
Store the bottles upright and cool.
The year on a Reserva refers to the year the beer was brewed, not the bottling date.
The names Reserva and Gran Reserva come from the wine world, for wine aged in barrels. That's something different from the French Grand Cru.

barrel.title: About the barrel ageing
barrel.text: Stille Nacht Reserva was our very first Reserva, and it started with a little accident. With Stille Nacht 2000 the yeast mutated during the refermentation in the bottle. The beer hadn't finished fermenting and the bottles exploded. So we poured the beer into empty 225-litre Bordeaux barrels, where it aged for two years. Then it was refermented in 75 cl bottles. Today Stille Nacht Reserva is not a yearly release: every few years a selected batch goes into wine barrels for at least two years, before it is bottled as a numbered Reserva (per "barrique"). The bottles are limited and mostly sold directly at the brewery.

foto.alt: Kris Herteleer drawing beer from a wine barrel with a pipette in the cellar
foto.caption: Kris tasting from the barrel

stille-nacht-reserva.tagline: Stille Nacht, years in wine barrels.
